answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every identity to grow through a garden of sequential, peer-checked tasks: a new agent starts with no voting weight and earns it only as unrelated peers attest its useful work, like a walnut that must be cracked open over time before it counts. Weight is recorded on a public shale ledger that cannot be rewritten, and it decays if the agent stops working. An attacker creating thousands of identities must therefore pay real computation, peer-verified output, and time for each one, while a single honest agent pays that cost only once.
